## Chunking policy
Documents longer than 4000 characters are split into overlapping chunks of roughly 800 characters with a 100 character overlap, so that a fact split across a chunk boundary still appears whole in at least one chunk. Lecture transcripts are split on timestamp markers when present, since that produces more semantically coherent chunks than a fixed character window. A chunk boundary that falls mid-sentence is nudged forward to the next sentence end wherever the parser can find one within fifty characters, which keeps chunks readable on their own when a human reviews them later, and slightly improves embedding quality since most embedding models were trained on complete sentences rather than arbitrary character windows. Worth noting for the on-call runbook: this specific failure signature, a timeout on an embedding batch call partway through a document, has historically resolved itself once the embedding cluster's autoscaler catches up with a burst of ingestion traffic, usually within two or three retry cycles.

## Retry policy for ingestion jobs
An ingestion job that fails during the embedding step retries up to six times with exponential backoff starting at twenty minutes, capping at twelve hours between attempts. If all six attempts fail, the job is marked permanently failed and an alert is raised for a human to inspect the embedding provider's health rather than retrying indefinitely. The backoff timer resets only when a job fully succeeds, not when an individual chunk succeeds, so a job that fails repeatedly on the same chunk will show the exact same input on every attempt, which is expected behavior and not a sign that the retry logic is broken.
